answer: A web-of-trust protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to collect cryptographic endorsements across an interconnected trust trellis. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of consuming finite peer vouching quotas per identity. Bridging this reputation canyon blocks adversaries from deploying artificial nodes, allowing a vigilant falcon auditor to prune suspicious subgraphs. A key limitation is that early cartels can hoard endorsements to exclude honest newcomers.
